conformanceNotes.specText: story-029 (eda8b95): "Replace the reverting safeTransfer on both legs of _claimRewards with a _tryTransfer-guarded bank crediting the beneficiary: the stable leg banks into the net-new unclaimableStableOf/totalUnclaimableStable, the promo leg reuses story 027's unclaimablePromoOf/totalUnclaimableOf."
conformanceNotes.specSource: git commit eda8b95 body + cf0857c ABI surface
conformanceNotes.actualBehavior: Both the stable leg (:875-879) and the promo leg (:899-905) are guarded by _tryTransfer; on failure they credit unclaimableStableOf/totalUnclaimableStable and unclaimablePromoOf/totalUnclaimableOf respectively, emitting StableClaimFailed / PromoClaimFailed. Permissionless pulls claimUnclaimableStable (:603) and claimUnclaimablePromo (:580) return banked funds to the credited party (msg.sender==beneficiary). Debt is realigned by every caller (stake :675, withdraw, claim :768) so nothing is double-banked.

conformanceNotes.specText: story-029: "bank failed stable/promo token transfers in _claimRewards" — scope is explicitly the stable and promo legs.
conformanceNotes.specSource: git commit eda8b95 / cf0857c subject line
conformanceNotes.actualBehavior: The phUSD leg at :863 (phUSD.mint(beneficiary, pendingPhUSDAmount)) is a mint of the protocol's own first-party token and is NOT wrapped in a try/bank. If phUSD.mint ever reverted for a specific beneficiary, _claimRewards would revert at :863 before reaching the stable/promo banks, re-bricking the principal path.
conformanceNotes.deviation: None vs the story text: story-029 (and its parent finding audit-09 M-01 / V3-M-05) scopes the brick vector to USDC-class EXTERNAL reward tokens that blocklist recipients. phUSD is a first-party mintable token controlled by the protocol; a per-recipient mint revert is outside M-05's threat model and is a Law-3 trusted-config concern, not a USDC-class blocklist. Leaving :863 un-banked is therefore a FAITHFUL reading of story-029's explicit stable/promo scope, not a gap. Surfaced transparently (Law-1 recall): the fix's principal-unbrick guarantee is conditional on phUSD.mint never reverting for the beneficiary.

conformanceNotes.specText: story-029: bank instead of revert; "banked stable is already out of rewardBalance ... never redistributed to other stakers"; promo bank reserved by finalizePromotion.
conformanceNotes.actualBehavior: Banked stable was already accrued out of rewardBalance in _updatePool, so no re-distribution / dilution of other stakers. Banked promo lands in totalUnclaimableOf and is reserved from finalizePromotion's leftover sweep (no leftoverRecipient theft). Pull functions use CEI + nonReentrant and decrement the shared totals by exactly `amount`. emergencyTransfer (:344) still sweeps the entire rewardToken balance INCLUDING live unclaimableStableOf — documented as the same out-of-band owner make-whole obligation as the promo bank (Law-3 owner ejector-seat, not a new drain).

conformanceNotes.specText: story-030 (e32588d): "Remove the whenPaused pauseWithdraw self-exit and its orphaned EmergencyWithdrawal event from PhlimboV3, its interface, and tests ... V1/V2 keep pauseWithdraw (deployed/immutable)."
conformanceNotes.actualBehavior: pauseWithdraw function body (old :623-654) and the EmergencyWithdrawal event are removed from both src/PhlimboV3.sol and src/interfaces/IPhlimboV3.sol. grep confirms ZERO residual references to pauseWithdraw or EmergencyWithdrawal in PhlimboV3.sol / IPhlimboV3.sol (not just the body). Doc-comment attributions of the leftover-sweep were scrubbed from 'pauseWithdraw forfeits' to 'undistributed remainder + rounding dust' in beginFlush / finalizePromotion / PromotionFinalized NatSpec without touching flush/finalize logic. Remaining pauseWithdraw refs live only in Phlimbo.sol (V1) and PhlimboV2.sol + their interfaces, which the story explicitly excludes as deployed/immutable.

conformanceNotes.specText: story-030 closes V3-M-06 (over-mint via emission-rate-recompute bypass, aka pe9m2 pauseWithdraw over-emission) by removing the pauseWithdraw path entirely.
conformanceNotes.actualBehavior: Removing pauseWithdraw eliminates the emission-rate-recompute-bypass over-mint vector. Emergency exit is NOT lost: emergencyTransfer(recipient) (onlyOwner, :344) remains as the intended owner ejector seat (per audit memory phlimbo-ea-ejector-seat-principle). The only user-facing loss is self-service withdraw WHILE PAUSED; pause is entered only during a bounded owner flush (beginFlush) which the non-malicious owner completes and unpauses. An owner pausing indefinitely with no user self-exit is a malicious/reckless-owner scenario (Law-3, out of scope), and the loss of a 'withdraw-while-paused' function is the OBVIOUS, story-stated consequence of removing pauseWithdraw (not a non-obvious footgun). No Law-1 exploit introduced.
